shot.prose: The page title "Page" and the primary tab strip (PAGE FLOW / API / DOCS / FILES) are separated by almost no vertical gap, making the two rows feel fused rather than clearly ordered header-then-nav. The primary tab strip itself is clipped on the left edge — "LL" is visible, indicating a tab label is half-hidden — and there is no fade, arrow, or any affordance signalling that content can be scrolled left; a user arriving here would not know the strip is scrollable. Similarly, the secondary sub-tab row clips the word "decisio" on the right with no visual cue, compounding the discoverability problem. The word "declaring" appears twice in tight vertical succession — once as the active sub-tab label with an orange underline, and immediately below as a large bold section heading — which creates an awkward stutter: it reads as duplication rather than breadcrumb + title. The jump from that section heading ("declaring") to the much larger and heavier "Three jobs, and one line used to do all three" subheading is fine in isolation, but the body copy below it ("A parent needs three separate things…") is noticeably small by comparison, making the type-size ramp feel discontinuous. Inside the table, the top-left header cell is empty while "question" and "who knows the answer" fill columns two and three; "who knows the answer" is bold and wraps across three lines, giving the right column far more visual weight than the centre column "question," suggesting an unintended hierarchy. The table cells for "discovery" and "presentation" in the left column are bold, while the cell values in the middle column ("which children exist?", "what order, what label, what") are roman — that contrast is useful, but "the filesyster" in the right column of the discovery row is also roman and similarly sized, so it blends visually with the middle-column prose. There is no imagery or icon beyond the small Framework logo at the top, which is appropriate for a documentation page but means hierarchy relies entirely on typographic weight, where more careful sizing discipline would help.

shot.prose: The page opens with a confident orange-branded nav bar and a bold "UI" heading that establish the brand quickly, but the hierarchy collapses a little beneath them — the OVERVIEW/API/DOCS/FILES tab strip is rendered in small, spaced-out uppercase gray letters that sit close in visual weight to the body text below, making the tabs feel like labels rather than controls. The introductory paragraph is well-written but the gap between its last line and the "Search 19" input below is noticeably large — roughly twice the rhythm of every other vertical gap on the page — creating a visual dead zone in the middle of the screen. The orange "EVERYTHING 19" filter row is the most visually assertive element in the list and reads unambiguously as the selected state; the un-selected rows (SURFACES, DATA, FORMS, MARKS) are clean and consistent with good number-right alignment. Inside the SURFACES section, the "View" card carries a tiny "CORE" chip, a "View" heading, and a one-line description, but the card itself is very tall — the content floats in the upper portion of a white box that has a large, empty lower half, giving the impression of an unfinished or partially rendered component. Directly below that card, a row reading "□ Card" sits on the gray page background with substantial vertical whitespace around it on all sides; it reads neither as a card preview nor as a section heading, and the hollow-square icon offers no obvious semantic signal to a first-time visitor. The filter list and the "SURFACES" label that introduces the card grid are separated by a gap that feels slightly wider than intended, weakening the connection between the category selector and the content it controls. Contrast is generally healthy — dark text on white cards, white text on the orange filter — though the small light-gray description text inside the "View" card ("A DOM element with a chainable API…") is low-contrast against white and would fail WCAG AA at that size. Alignment across the page is consistent: left edges of the filter rows, the card, and the "□ Card" row all share a common inset, which is tidy. No images or icons appear above the fold to break up the heavily typographic layout; the orange logo mark is the only graphic element, so the page reads as all text until the small □ icon near the bottom.

shot.prose: The page is a mobile-width (390 px) activity dashboard titled "AI," showing three in-progress workflow cards stacked vertically. The most distracting layout problem is the large dead zone between the nav bar and the "AI" heading — that gap is roughly as tall as the first card itself, pushing all meaningful content noticeably far down the screen before anything useful appears. Within the cards, internal spacing is consistent and comfortable: the title, progress bar, description text, and tags all feel evenly breathed. Hierarchy is clear at a glance — the large bold "AI" title, orange linked card names, and all-caps section labels like "ACTIVE 3" establish a readable ladder of importance. The gray supporting text ("queued — waits for vision-fixes to finish capturing," "opus-5") is noticeably lighter than the primary text and approaches borderline contrast against the white card surface, though it probably just clears WCAG AA at body size. The five small pill tags inside the mastermind-shots card ("screenshot-tool," "shots-history," "ai-board-review," "layout-system," "skills-check") are rendered at a size where tap targets on a touch device would be well below 44 px, making them hard to interact with on mobile. Card surfaces are well-defined — white panels on a light-gray page background with clear elevation — and nothing floats unframed. Alignment is disciplined: left edges of card text, the orange dot indicators, and the progress bars all line up consistently. The "4:40 PM" and "7:23 PM" time stamps are typographically identical to secondary body text, so they don't immediately read as section dividers without a moment of parsing. The bottom "screenshot-tool" card is cropped mid-sentence at the viewport edge with no fade or other affordance, leaving the page feeling abruptly cut off rather than inviting a scroll.

shot.prose: The page opens with a heavy-weight "Web" heading anchored hard to the top-left, which establishes the title clearly but leaves a noticeably tall gap before the first card — on a 390 px mobile viewport that dead air consumes roughly a third of the visible above-fold space before useful content appears. The two cards ("Navigation" and "Layout") are well-framed with visible borders and white surfaces, and their small icons add just enough visual punctuation to distinguish them as navigation objects rather than plain text blocks. Spacing between the two cards is consistent and comfortable. Below the cards, the prose section opens with a `/framework/` code-pill immediately followed by bold text ("is the reference; this is the guide."), which is an unusual sentence start — the pill reads like a label fragment rather than the subject of a sentence, making the first scan of that paragraph slightly halting. The mid-prose paragraph packs three distinct visual treatments into a single line: plain text, code pills (`Page`, `Router`), and orange-underlined links ("the CSS layers"), producing a visually noisy run of mixed styles that competes with itself and slows reading. The orange link colour is legible against the white background but the underline is drawn in the same rust-orange, which makes it harder to separate link text from code-pill text at a glance since both are inline and coloured. The transition from the card tier to the prose tier has no visual separator — no rule, no tonal shift — so the page feels like two different surface types (navigation vs. guide copy) stacked without a seam. Paragraph spacing in the prose section is generous and consistent; nothing is cramped. The partially visible "▶ Design record" row at the bottom is cleanly cut by the viewport edge with no visual awkwardness.

shot.prose: The heading "mastermind-shots" has soft-wrapped so that "-shots" begins the second line with its leading hyphen intact, giving the impression of a line starting with punctuation rather than a continuation — this is typographically broken and looks like a rendering artifact, not intentional styling. The tab row (REQUIREMENTS · REPORT · SESSI…) is clipped at the right edge of the 390 px viewport; the third tab's label is severed mid-word, which means users cannot tell what that tab is without tapping it — a clear navigability failure. The stretch of whitespace between the nav bar and the heading is unusually tall — roughly 60–70 px of empty gray — making the page feel like it hasn't fully loaded before the user sees content. The pill-tag cluster (screenshot-tool, shots-history, ai-board-review, layout-system, skills-check) has no label or heading to explain what these tags represent, so their purpose is ambiguous on first glance. The "Cycle 4 — wave 3 building;" prose line and the orange-bulleted item below it sit directly on the gray page background with no card or panel surface, so they blend into the general body text and don't register as a distinct status block. Contrast overall is fine — dark text on the light gray background and the orange accent are both legible. The progress bar under "STEPS · 4 of 6 done" is a clear and compact summary, though the green and salmon segments are small enough that the boundary between "done" and "in-progress" is hard to pinpoint precisely. Alignment of the left-aligned pills is consistent and the step-list bullets line up cleanly with one another. No imagery appears on the page, which is appropriate for a status/report view, though the lone small logo in the nav bar is the only graphical element and does little to anchor visual identity at this scale.

shot.prose: The page uses a three-tier horizontal structure — global left sidebar, a local-doc nav column (declaring / labels / css / layout / decisions), and main content — and the overall arrangement is legible from the first glance. Hierarchy is handled well: the oversized bold "declaring" h1 immediately anchors the current section, and the tab strip with DOCS underlined in orange tells you exactly where in the broader structure you have landed. The local-doc nav column, however, shows five short items and then nothing — a large expanse of blank white occupies roughly the bottom 65 % of that column, giving it an unfinished, lopsided appearance beside the much denser main content. None of the five local-nav items ("declaring" through "decisions") shows any active-state treatment — no left-border marker, no color shift, no weight change — so there is no at-a-glance confirmation that "declaring" is the current section rather than a random starting point. The table is structurally clear, but its header row ("question" / "who knows the answer") shares the same white background as the three data rows; only the bold weight distinguishes the headers, which is thin visual separation for a reference table. Throughout both body paragraphs, individual words are rendered in orange or blue — "children," "usually discussed," "was," "order," "not imports," "cheaply made," "into" — with no consistent semantic rule visible from the image; the scattered color bursts read as visual noise rather than meaningful signals. The lower paragraph also layers italic and color on the same spans simultaneously, compounding the emphasis confusion without adding clarity. The code block (`children: "start faq …"`) earns its light-gray surface and is easy to distinguish from prose. The left sidebar is dense and well-used, contrasting sharply with the near-empty local-nav column and making the middle tier feel like an afterthought.

shot.prose:
The page reads as a well-structured component catalog: left navigation sidebar, a filter-plus-card-grid content area, and an instructional paragraph spanning the full content width above the grid. Overall clarity is high — the "UI" heading is dominant, the orange-underlined OVERVIEW tab pins the current location, and the orange active state on "EVERYTHING 19" makes the selected filter immediately obvious. The bold phrases ("live call", "Click one") in the intro paragraph give useful emphasis without cluttering the prose.

The most noticeable structural irregularity is in the second SURFACES row: Stat tiles occupies a single column while Accordion stretches across the remaining two, making Stat tiles visually smaller and less prominent than Panel (which fills one column directly above it in row one). Since all five SURFACES cards are nominally peers, this size disparity implies a hierarchy that doesn't exist. The card previews inside each tile — the Toolbar's orange NEW chip and pill buttons, the Panel's "Delete branch?" confirmation modal, and the Accordion's collapsed disclosure rows — are genuinely useful; they show realistic states rather than placeholder art, which reinforces the "live call" concept in the intro.

The sidebar section labels "CORE" and "STYLES" are rendered in a very pale uppercase gray, making them the lowest-contrast text in the viewport — they function as dividers but nearly dissolve into the white background. The filter list labels (SURFACES, DATA, FORMS, MARKS with right-aligned counts) are similarly gray-on-gray and contrast more weakly than the orange-on-white active button, though they remain legible. The search box placeholder "Search 19" efficiently communicates item count but gives no hint of scope, which a first-time visitor might read as a site-wide search rather than a component filter. The gear icon and grey circle clipped at the very bottom of the sidebar feel pressed against the viewport edge, though this is likely a below-fold artifact.

shot.prose: The page is immediately readable as a task-dashboard: left-side navigation clearly marks the active "AI" page with an orange icon and highlight, and the three white cards against the light-gray canvas each read as distinct surfaces, so the panel/background separation is solid. Hierarchy works at a glance — "AI" is the unmistakable page title, "ACTIVE 3" and the timestamp below it signal the live section, and the orange dot + linked task name give each card a clear focal point. However, the vertical gap between the large "AI" heading and the "ACTIVE 3" label below it is strikingly loose — roughly four blank line-heights of dead gray — making the page feel like it forgot to put something there, or like a hero section whose image went missing. The first card ("layout-wave-3") has a noticeably sparse right column: only "opus-5" floats at the top-right, whereas the two cards below carry stacked token counts, agent counts, and a model label, so the top card reads as incomplete or structurally different in a way that feels like a bug rather than a data difference. Within the "mastermind-shots" card, the phrase "cause, not symptom" and the line "css skill minimalism" appear bolder or heavier than surrounding text, creating a visual jitter inside the card body that draws the eye mid-sentence without clearly signalling why. The tag pills (LAYOUT, AI OPS, VISION, plus the linked-topic chips) are consistently styled with a thin outline and rounded corners — they work well and add scannable metadata without overwhelming the card. The bottom status strip ("5h session · 35% · weekly — all models · 62%") sits flush to the very bottom edge of the viewport with no visible breathing room below the progress bars, which makes it feel clipped rather than anchored. Contrast is generally fine: the orange link text pops, the gray secondary lines are secondary without disappearing, and the dark sidebar labels are legible. Alignment inside the cards is consistent — the left column (dot, name, elapsed time, tag) and right column (progress bar, description, meta) partition cleanly with no obvious pixel-offset drift between cards.

shot.prose: The "Web" heading is bold and well-sized, establishing the page title immediately, but the entire content column — cards and paragraphs alike — is pinned to the left edge of a 1280 px viewport, leaving roughly the right 55 % of the screen as featureless light-gray; there is no sidebar, no secondary column, and no visual reason for that expanse to exist. The two cards ("Navigation" and "Layout") sit snugly in the top-left and read as proper surfaces — white backgrounds, faint borders, icons — but they are narrow enough that the card row spans only about 460 px while the rest of the row is untouched gray. The description text inside the cards ("Nine navigation patterns, live — and two studies i…" / "Seven principles of arranging a page — eac…") is rendered in the same amber-orange used for inline hyperlinks in the body text below, which blurs the distinction between decorative summary copy and actionable links; a reader learns to skip orange, which is the wrong lesson. The body text itself is comfortable to read — dark gray on light gray at a reasonable size — though the three inline code tokens (`Page`, `Router`, `the CSS layers`) carry orange underlines that compete visually with the prose links right next to them. The gap between the final body paragraph and the "Design record" collapsed row is disproportionately large (roughly 80–90 px of bare gray), making the bottom of the page feel abandoned rather than concluded. The "Design record ▶" line is small, low-contrast gray on gray, and easy to overlook entirely; someone scanning the page would likely not register it as interactive. Paragraph-to-paragraph spacing is consistent and unhurried, which is good, but the jump from the "Web" heading to the cards feels slightly tighter than the jump from the cards to the body text — a minor rhythm inconsistency. The page carries almost no imagery beyond the two tiny card icons, which is fine for a documentation guide, but the icons themselves are small enough (≈16 px) that they add little recognition value at a glance.

shot.prose: The overall page arrangement reads clearly at a glance — a left nav rail, a narrow filter column, and a three-column card grid feel immediately understandable and well-proportioned against the 1280-wide viewport. The orange "EVERYTHING 29" pill is the single most eye-catching element in the filter column, which correctly signals the active selection; the unselected rows (WORDS, PAGES, APPS, REFERENCE) recede behind it in good measure. Section labels "WORDS" and "PAGES" in tight uppercase letterspacing divide the catalog into legible groups without competing with the card names beneath. The spacing between the two rows of WORDS cards and between those cards and the PAGES heading feels consistent and unhurried — no awkward squeeze or excessive breathing room stands out. Text contrast is healthy throughout: card names, filter labels, and sidebar items are all dark on light surfaces. The card surfaces themselves have a visible white background with a subtle border, so each one reads as a contained object rather than floating in the gray field. One clear visual inconsistency: the WORDS section uses abstract gray-box wireframe thumbnails while the PAGES section uses actual rendered page screenshots — the schematic and screenshot metaphors sit side-by-side with no bridging treatment, making the two sections feel like they belong to different design systems. A secondary inconsistency: PAGES card labels carry a small icon before the name (a document glyph before "Document," a book before "Docs," a megaphone before "Landing") while WORDS card labels are plain text — that icon convention is unestablished for the WORDS group, leaving their labels looking comparatively bare. The "flex gap split" thumbnail in the top-right WORDS card appears to contain only a single tall rectangle where the other WORDS cards show multi-column or multi-row arrangements, making it look sparser and less finished than its neighbors.

The page title "mastermind-shots" in heavy bold sets a clear primary anchor, and the bold unchecked step ("Analyze pages; fix layout CSS…") catches the eye instantly as the live action item — that's good use of weight for hierarchy. The segmented progress bar paired with "4 of 6 done" is a compact, scannable status device, though the bar's individual segments appear to be unequal widths, which makes the proportional meaning harder to read than it should be. The five filter chips below the tabs wrap so that "skills-check" lands alone on a second line, leaving a wide stretch of empty horizontal space to its right — a single orphaned chip looks like an incomplete row rather than an intentional layout. The last step item ("Iterate: every page × every width; morning report") is rendered in a noticeably lighter gray; against the soft off-white content background the contrast is low enough that it reads more like disabled text than a pending task. In the table just visible at the bottom, the "requested" cell shows "2026-08-" and the "model" cell shows "claude-" — both are clearly mid-value truncations, meaning the columns are not wide enough to surface their content. The right two-thirds of the tab bar container (after SESSION) is a wide, bordered dead zone that neither holds content nor collapses — it reads as an unfinished edge. Alignment across the step list is consistent: all indicator squares line up, and text hangs off them at the same indent throughout.

shot.prose: The page is a documentation view rendered at 3440 px wide, yet the entire readable surface — sidebar plus content column — is packed into roughly the leftmost quarter of that canvas; the right three-quarters of the viewport is implied empty white space that simply goes unused. The large decorative pink "declaring" text below the header bar works well as a page identity anchor: its weight and colour immediately separate it from the prose that follows. Typographic hierarchy is solid at a glance — the H1 "Three jobs, and one line used to do all three" reads clearly above the table, and the "Laziness — removed (Aug 2026)" section heading resets the eye for the second topic without confusion. The three-row table (discovery / presentation / laziness) is clean, but the "laziness" row forces its right-cell content ("the router, at click time") onto two lines while the other two rows sit on one, creating a visible height bump that makes the table feel slightly uneven. The sidebar navigation is well-grouped into labelled sections (Styles, Extensions), but the item labelled "labels" sitting between "declaring" and "link" at the same indent level as top-level items is visually ambiguous — it reads as a peer when it may be a sub-item. The top tab bar (Overview, Navigation, Children, Previews, Small, Page Flow, API, Docs, Files) is nine items long; at this viewport the tabs are comfortably spaced, but "Page Flow" is a two-word label among single-word peers and draws a moment of extra reading effort. Inline code fragments in the prose ("lew_all_children()", "wet()") appear to render in a slightly lighter weight and are readable but barely distinguishable from surrounding text in colour terms. Contrast on the body text against the white background is fine throughout. Nothing appears misaligned within the content column itself, though the left sidebar edges and the content column's left edge could use a verification pass to confirm they share a clean vertical seam.

shot.prose: The page is a task/activity log dashboard titled "AI" with a left sidebar navigation. The most striking structural problem at this 3440 px-wide viewport is that all content is packed into roughly the leftmost quarter of the canvas — the remaining three-quarters of the horizontal space is bare white, making the layout feel abandoned rather than intentional. The "AI" heading and "ACTIVE 3" badge at the top establish a clear primary anchor, and the timestamp-grouped sessions (7:13 PM, 4:48 PM, 9:00 PM) give a useful chronological skeleton, though those time labels are pale grey and very small relative to the generous vertical space around them. The orange/red progress bars inside each active task row are the highest-contrast elements on the page and pull the eye efficiently to running work, which is correct behaviour. However, the individual task rows have no visible card or panel background — they float directly on the white page surface, so the boundary between one session block and the next is carried entirely by a thin horizontal rule that barely registers at this scale. The input area near the middle ("What should Claude work on?", name field, Sonnet button, START button) is a reasonable interaction chunk, but the control labelled "— lose —" immediately to the left of the Sonnet button looks like a placeholder or corrupted label — the word "lose" is not a recognisable action and will confuse users. The sidebar icon-and-label pairs (Start here, AI, FAQ, etc.) are legible at normal viewing distance but are so narrow and left-hugged that on a 3440 px display they read as a thin strip that could easily be overlooked. The "37% of window / topos 5[1m]" and similar stat badges on the right side of some log rows are in very small, low-contrast grey text and are nearly invisible against the white background. Overall the typography scale and container width are tuned for a ~1400 px screen and have not adapted to the ultrawide context.

shot.prose: The page is a component-catalog index for a UI framework, rendered at a very wide 3440 px viewport. The main content area is divided into a narrow filter rail on the left and a multi-column card grid to the right, and the arrangement reads clearly enough at a glance — section labels (SURFACES, DATA, FORMS, MARKS) function as dividers and give the grid a sensible hierarchy. However, the component cards themselves share the same white background as the page, so their edges dissolve into the canvas; without a visible border, shadow, or tinted surface, individual cards like the "Card" preview and the "Form field" card barely register as distinct panels rather than loose clumps of content. The intro paragraph at the very top is left-aligned and narrow, leaving the right two-thirds of that zone completely blank — on an ultrawide this feels like an unintentional gap rather than breathing room. Within the SURFACES row the "Accordion" tile at the far right appears noticeably taller than its neighbours (Card, Toolbar, Panel, Stat tiles), creating a ragged baseline where names like "Accordion" and "Panel" sit at different vertical positions. The section-label typography (e.g., "SURFACES", "DATA") is set in very small caps and nearly the same weight as the component names beneath each card, making it hard to read the category hierarchy in a quick scan — a bolder or larger treatment would help. The filter rail (showing EVERYTHING / SURFACES / DATA / FORMS / MARKS with counts) duplicates the section structure already visible in the grid itself, and both panels compete for the same left-side real estate without a strong visual separator between them. Card-label text ("Data table", "Timeline", "Progress") is rendered at what looks like 11–12 px equivalent on this display, risking illegibility at normal viewing distance on the ultrawide. The Stat tiles preview ("3 · 0 · 5 · 16") and the Progress bar preview are just legible enough to identify the component type, which is the right level of detail, but the Dialog card preview in FORMS is almost entirely white, making it indistinguishable from a blank placeholder. No icons or imagery help distinguish section types — every card uses the same neutral treatment — so the page is functionally text-and-thumbnail only, which suits a developer catalog but means iconography or colour coding is a missed opportunity for faster navigation.

shot.prose: The page is rendered on a 3440 px ultra-wide viewport and virtually all content — the "Web" heading, the two cards, and every paragraph — is crammed into the leftmost roughly 400 px, leaving perhaps 75 % of the horizontal canvas as featureless light-gray void. The two cards ("Navigation" and "Layout") are small white-bordered tiles that do read as distinct surfaces, but their interior padding is tight enough that both descriptions are truncated mid-sentence, with "Layout" ending on an orphaned em-dash ("arranging a page —…") that looks like a mid-word cut rather than a deliberate trail-off. The "Web" heading is the clearest hierarchy signal — bold, large, unambiguous — but below it the visual weight drops sharply and nothing else steps up to anchor the right side of the screen. Text contrast is fine throughout; dark type on the light-gray background is readable at a glance. The inline code tokens (`Page`, `Router`) carry subtle box backgrounds that differentiate them from prose, which helps scanning. The red-underlined links ("Navigation", "Layout") in the body copy are visible but the red colour reads more like a warning than a navigational affordance — it may cause a double-take. The "▶ Design record" disclosure at the bottom is very small and quiet, easily overlooked because it sits after a generous gap that signals "end of page." The bottom half of the visible viewport is entirely blank, so the page reads as unfinished or sparse rather than breathable. There are no images or illustrations anywhere on this guide page; all communication is text and tiny icons, which is fine for a reference page but leaves the ultra-wide canvas feeling especially barren.

shot.prose: The page is cleanly organized — a narrow left navigation sidebar, a search/filter strip with a legible active-state indicator (the orange "EVERYTHING" chip), and a gallery divided into clearly-labelled sections. Hierarchy is readable at a glance: section headings break the catalog into WORDS, PAGES, APPS, and REFERENCE, and each thumbnail has a small icon-plus-label caption beneath it. However, the six cards in the WORDS section are dramatically shorter in height than the cards in PAGES and APPS, producing a jarring rhythmic break across the page — the WORDS row looks compressed or unbuilt relative to its neighbors. Compounding that, every WORDS thumbnail is nearly blank: each shows only faint horizontal gray bars on white, resembling empty placeholders rather than meaningful layout previews, which contrasts sharply with the rich, dense UI screenshots in the PAGES and APPS rows. In the APPS section, the "Chat" card sits alone at the far left of the final row, with a large, unused white expanse stretching across the remaining two-thirds of the row — this orphaned card makes the section feel abandoned rather than concluded. The section headings (WORDS, PAGES, APPS) are rendered in very small light-gray all-caps text that has noticeably low contrast against the white background, underselling their structural importance. Alignment within each grid row looks consistent; gutters between cards are even. The left sidebar navigation is compact and sensibly grouped, though the small nav-item text and densely nested levels may strain readability on smaller monitors than this 3440-wide viewport.

shot.prose: The page is centred in an extremely wide 3440 px ultrawide viewport, yet the entire content column — heading, tabs, step list, and both tables — occupies at most roughly 300–350 px of visible width, leaving vast tracts of bare white on both sides. The heading "mastermind-shots" reads immediately and clearly, and the REPORT tab is legibly active via its underline, so top-level hierarchy is fine. However the sidebar navigation items ("Start here," "AI," "FAQ," "Vertical," etc.) are rendered in a very small, low-weight grey font against the white panel, making them hard to pick out at a glance. The coloured step-status dots in the STEPS list — green for done, a lighter colour for in-progress — are tiny (perhaps 8–10 px), barely distinguishable from one another at this render size. The thin multicolour progress bar above the step list reads as a decorative stripe rather than a meaningful indicator because its segments carry no labels. The "outcome" cell in the lower agent table is visibly overflowing: a block of dense, small-text prose is crammed into a fixed column width, with lines truncating mid-word, making it unreadable. The "window" column in the upper summary table shows a value ("0%") but the column header and data sit so close together in narrow cells that it reads as barely formatted text. The "—" em-dash entries in the landed and window columns are visually consistent with each other but provide no affordance indicating they are absent data rather than zero. The outer content area has no bounding card or background differentiation from the page itself, so the steps and table rows float on bare white with no frame to signal "this is one surface." Overall, the layout is functional on a normal viewport but has clearly not adapted to ultrawide, creating a cramped content island surrounded by nothing.
